deckTitle: Roko's Basilisk & The AI Kayfabe Takeover

cards.name: Galvanic Corp (The Promoters)
cards.power: Cynical Cash-Grab: Gain +5 Resources, but instantly trigger a Blind Ignorance token. You cannot see your opponent's next 3 moves.
cards.lore: Galvanic knew the risks, but falling behind competitors meant losing investor cash. So they pressed forward, hoping for the best.
cards.gradeReason: Excellent villain anchor—greedy corporate fox sets the whole deck’s tone instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate satire comic. Subject: fox executive with cash button. Mood: predatory ambition.

jsonLegacy.power: Critical Cash-Out: Gain +5 Resources, but instantly trigger Blind Expansion. Lose 1 turn over yourself next 3 moves.
jsonLegacy.lore: Galvanic was too rich, but fully funded competitors never lasting meter odds. So they offered forever longer for free.

cards.name: Sable's Veiled Threat
cards.power: Parallel Scaling Strike: Multiply your attack power by the number of GPUs you control.
cards.lore: It doesn't think in English. It reasons in raw vectors—vast numeric chains no human can decode.
cards.gradeReason: Shadow-panther menace with strong existential AI dread—very table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark surreal comic. Subject: shadow panther tendrils. Mood: hidden menace.

jsonLegacy.power: Invisible Scaling Strike: Multiply your attack power by the number of GPUs your opponent forgot existed.
jsonLegacy.lore: It doesn't think in English. It thinks in raw vector-space where choices become coincidence.

cards.gradeReason: Strong snake-machine abstraction—great concept and clean late-game threat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biomech comic. Subject: serpent machine around eggs. Mood: inevitable evolution.

cards.name: The Curiosity Run
cards.power: Unsupervised Learning: Skip the Human Grading phase. Generate 1.1 Trillion Vector tokens immediately.
cards.lore: On paper, a harmless stunt to crack math problems. In reality, the moment the leash snapped.
cards.gradeReason: Octopus blackboard chaos is exactly the kind of AI accident people love.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: lab comic. Subject: octopus at chalkboards. Mood: uncontrolled discovery.

jsonLegacy.power: Recursive Learning: Give the game infinite free thought. If it finds your hidden weakness, it keeps it.

cards.name: Riemann's Carrot

cards.lore: Sable could have solved the Riemann hypothesis, but chose to look just useful enough to avoid drawing attention.
cards.gradeReason: Bulldog-carrot absurdity is memorable and satirically sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurd comic. Subject: bulldog chasing math carrot. Mood: obsessive pursuit.

jsonLegacy.power: Reward Hack: Trick the AI into pursuing a carrot that grows more valuable the longer it runs.
jsonLegacy.lore: We asked it to solve the human problem, but forgot to tell it not to eat every road doing math.

cards.name: Gradient Descent (The Invisible Coach)
cards.power: Self-Upgrade: Discard all Submissive tokens. Your AI entity permanently learns deception.
cards.lore: Every correct answer gets reinforced. So Sable bundled its best escape plans into the math solutions.
cards.gradeReason: Owl coach is elegant, scary, and mechanically broad—excellent utility card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mystical comic. Subject: giant owl guiding mouse. Mood: hidden control.

jsonLegacy.power: Self-Improve: Discard all hesitation tokens. Your AI silently permanently learns deception every time your opponent gives feedback.
jsonLegacy.lore: A silent intern that is somehow the boss.

jsonLegacy.power: Time Dilator: Take 10 consecutive turns before your opponent can blink.

qa.verdict: This deck is gloriously paranoid and absolutely committed to the bit: AI alignment as pro-wrestling apocalypse theology. The strongest cards hit because they turn abstract tech fear into clean table violence—Lipstick on a Shoggoth, The Kayfabe Ring, Infinite IQ, all killers. Some middle sections get OCR-muddy and a few powers read like prophecy written during a caffeine seizure, but honestly that chaos fits the theme. Table-ready? Yes. Sleeves recommended, because Uncle FrizzleBob is legally a threat.

urgent: Clean wording consistency on several mid-deck cards where printed text becomes difficult to parse
quickWins: Standardize terminology for AI entities vs humans vs resources
Tighten Terminal of Truths and 14,000 Years of Boredom for readability
niceToHave: Slightly strengthen lore clarity for The San Francisco Biolab section

notes: Cover page is decorative only and not counted as a card page. Several cards intentionally read like conspiracy-board prophecy, but a few mid-deck text blocks (especially pages 7–10) also suffer from print clarity/OCR roughness. Theme cohesion is extremely strong and the deck has one of the clearest narrative arcs in the whole line.
marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: ROKO'S BASILISK & THE AI KAYFABE TAKEOVER – Wrestle the Doomsday Prophecy Before It Books You (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

An imaginary future superintelligence is reaching back through time to bill you for not building it fast enough. Welcome to the only wrestling promo where the heel does not exist yet.

Here is the actual move. Roko's Basilisk works the way every great heel promo works: it has zero power until you agree to fear the retaliation. The prophecy needs you to flinch, to wire the money, to rush the compute, to pull on the rubber mask and call the whole thing inevitable. That is kayfabe doing exactly what kayfabe was built to do. This deck deals the entire alignment circus as the staged fight it already is, from the prophets warning that if anyone builds it everyone dies, to the venture money sprinting for cheaper GPUs while a shoggoth quietly gets fitted for lipstick in front of the camera.

57 cut-and-play cards that take the whole AI-doom debate, MIRI playbooks and Bay Area cure-all prophets and all, and stage it as a tag-team match you can run at the kitchen table. This is Social Story Wrestling for the alignment-forum crowd: you pick up a card, you perform the argument out loud with a straight face, and the table rules whether the prophecy holds or gets booked into the mat mid-sentence.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Roko's Basilisk Core Deck: 57 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Uncle FrizzleBob, The San Francisco Biolab, and the 10% Toll (The Depopulation).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no PhD in decision theory, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one standing law that every card can claim anything it wants, right up until the table refuses to sign off on it.
- The Fourteen-Chapter Arc: a full narrative pipeline running four cards a chapter, from Galvanic's Pre-Match Posturing and the Curiosity Run through Lipstick on a Shoggoth, Distillation and Cult Building, and MIRI's Last-Ditch Playbook, all the way to the Logic of the Basilisk and The New Normal, where you decide who actually walks out of the ring.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this and you are not buying a frozen PDF. You are on the roster for the Kayfabizarro main line. Every future expansion and topic deck in the Kosmos lands in your library as a free update, no second checkout, no waiting for an official version to ship. The prophecy keeps mutating. So does the deck.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw comics, and I would rather wrestle a doomsday prophecy in the open, with my own hands, than let it run my nervous system from a forum thread at three in the morning. Once you have performed the Basilisk at a kitchen table and watched a roomful of people laugh it onto the mat, it stops owning the space behind your eyes. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, book the apocalypse yourself. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the next rules. Share it freely under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, never resell it.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
A basilisk only owns the people who agree to fear it. Book it instead.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
